atlas-lu.0001: One Luxembourg recruiter estimated in April 2026 that 50% of positions require French, German or Luxembourgish and that English accounts for the other 50% of requirements; the Big Four call English and French essential.
atlas-lu.0002: The Big Four’s hiring in Luxembourg peaks in September and January and covers both graduates and experienced people.
atlas-lu.0003: The European Investment Bank takes trainees in two intakes a year, in March-April and September-October, announced about 4 months ahead.
atlas-lu.0004: Employment in Luxembourg passed 530,000 in March 2026 and about 143,000 new contracts were signed in 2025, though vacancies remain well below their post-pandemic highs.
atlas-lu.0005: ADEM reports unemployment of 6.2% at the end of 2025 and 6.3% at the end of March 2026, with more than 21,000 resident job seekers registered.
atlas-lu.0006: Europe’s largest investment-fund centre, with about €9 trillion in fund assets, so the graduate market is fund administration, asset management, banking and the professional services around them, plus several EU institutions. Work is multilingual; English is common in finance.
atlas-lu.0009: Employment in the fund industry itself and entry pay by employer were not read: Eurostat counts finance and insurance jobs as a whole, and ALFI publishes assets, not jobs, on the page used.
atlas-lu.0010: All immigration, visa and registration rules are consolidated from primary sources in visas_immigration/luxembourg/luxembourg_visas_immigration_guide.md.
atlas-lu.0011: Tax and net pay were not researched for this record.
atlas-lu.0012: Cross-border commuters, who fill a large share of Luxembourg’s jobs, and the University of Luxembourg’s size and ranking were not read on a primary page (its site could not be read).
atlas-lu.0013: The pay metric is the national mean from the 2022 structure-of-earnings survey (all employees of firms with 10 or more staff), not a figure for graduates or for the city alone.
atlas-lu.0016: Fund administration, asset management and private-markets back offices
atlas-lu.0018: €6.69 trillion in UCITS and €9.07 trillion including AIFs
atlas-lu.0020: more than 4,000 employees in Luxembourg and in offices around the world
atlas-lu.0023: Luxembourg-domiciled UCITS funds held €6.69 trillion of net assets in June 2026, €9.07 trillion including alternative funds, up about 20% in twelve months.
atlas-lu.0024: Expats rank Luxembourg 4th in the 2026 Working Abroad Index and 1st for job security.
atlas-lu.0025: In 2022 employees under 30 in Luxembourg firms with 10 or more staff (public administration excluded) earned a mean of €48,369 gross a year, and those under 30 working as professionals €60,726, against €74,542 for all ages.
atlas-lu.0026: In 2025 the employment rate of Luxembourg residents aged 20 to 34 with a tertiary degree was 90.5% (88.2% for those who finished within the last five years); unemployment was 6.5% overall, 21.6% for the 15-to-24s in 2024, and GDP was €89.5 billion.
atlas-lu.0027: The Global Financial Centres Index 40 (September 2026) ranks Luxembourg 17th in the world (down 1 place) and fourth in Western Europe after London, Zurich and Geneva; in the investment-management sector table it is second in the world, behind Hong Kong, and it is 12th for banking.
atlas-lu.0028: Luxembourg has 510,990 jobs (2023): 115,420 of them in public administration, defence, education and health, 90,490 in professional, scientific, technical and administrative services, 54,220 in finance and insurance and 22,730 in information and communication.
atlas-lu.0029: Of the 152 metropolitan regions for which Eurostat publishes jobs by sector (latest year, 2021 or 2022; German, British and Swiss regions are not in the table), Luxembourg has the 11th-most jobs in finance and insurance (53,040, just behind Brussels with 63,000) and the 45th-most in information and communication (21,830).
atlas-lu.0030: The European Investment Bank says it has more than 4,000 employees in Luxembourg and in offices around the world.
atlas-lu.0031: The CSSF, Luxembourg’s financial-sector supervisor, says it has over 950 employees working in many specialised departments.
atlas-lu.0032: Startup Genome’s 2026 report puts the value of Luxembourg’s start-up ecosystem at $4 billion (Europe’s average $14.3 billion), with $271 million of seed and Series A funding in H2 2023–2025 and $1 billion of exits in 2021–2025.
atlas-lu.0033: Luxembourg recruits from abroad by necessity: about 47% of employees commute from France, Belgium and Germany. Graduate hiring is dominated by the Big Four and the fund industry, which take large intakes every year, mostly from internships and graduate applications.
atlas-lu.0034: There is no national season, but the large firms hire in waves: the Big Four peak in September and January, and the European Investment Bank takes trainees in two intakes a year.
atlas-lu.0036: The four firms employ about 9,100 people in Luxembourg; in 2022 their recruitment targets ran from about 500 to 910 each.
atlas-lu.0037: Hiring peaks in September and January and targets graduates as well as experienced people; Deloitte and KPMG use online assessments of analytical skills followed by several interviews. English and French are described as essential.
atlas-lu.0039: A practical internship needs an agreement and is open to enrolled students and to people who finished secondary school or a first higher-education cycle (Bachelor, BTS); in the last two cases the whole internship must fall within 12 months after the last enrolment. It cannot exceed 6 months in 24 with the same host.
atlas-lu.0040: Pay is set by law: from 4 weeks, at least 40% of the unskilled minimum social wage for 4 to 12 weeks and 75% for over 12 to 26 weeks; for holders of a Bachelor or BTS the reference is the skilled minimum wage.
atlas-lu.0042: Applications go through employer portals and boards such as jobs.lu, which lists a "Graduate" and an "Internship" category and shows the vacancies in English, French and German. In 2025 the national employment agency ADEM passed more than 123,000 candidate profiles to employers and organised 106 job fairs.
atlas-lu.0043: Moovijob Day, held on 20 March 2026 at Luxexpo The Box, had more than 150 companies confirmed and is open to anyone, including students, for jobs and internships.
atlas-lu.0044: EU institutions and the civil service
atlas-lu.0045: The European Investment Bank takes trainees in two intakes a year, March-April and September-October, announced about 4 months ahead; they must be in their final year or have less than 1 year of work experience, be EU or candidate-country nationals and be proficient in English and/or French.
atlas-lu.0046: The state recruits civil servants by competitive exam: candidates must be nationals of an EU state and show sufficient Luxembourgish, French and German; in general administration the general aptitude test stays valid for 5 years, and posts are listed on GovJobs.lu.
atlas-lu.0047: The job market has softened since the post-pandemic peak: ADEM reports unemployment of 6.2% at the end of 2025 and 6.3% at the end of March 2026, and vacancies well below their earlier highs, although employment passed 530,000 in March 2026 and about 143,000 new contracts were signed in 2025.
atlas-lu.0048: Fund administration, depositary, compliance and risk work hire juniors in large numbers and train them; English is the main working language in the financial sector.
atlas-lu.0049: The Big Four are among the country’s largest employers, about 9,100 people, and take hundreds of graduates a year into audit and advisory, many of them from France, Belgium and Germany.
atlas-lu.0050: The European Investment Bank (more than 4,000 staff in Luxembourg and worldwide) and the financial supervisor CSSF (over 950 staff, recruiting from entry level to senior) are the main public-interest employers for finance graduates.
atlas-lu.0051: IT roles sit mostly in banks, fund administrators and the Big Four, which need people who understand both regulation and systems; English is enough in most of them.
atlas-lu.0052: No single school is the gate: employers draw on graduates from France, Belgium, Germany and well beyond, so the degree and the language mix count more than a school ranking.
atlas-lu.0053: Moovijob Day (20 March 2026, Luxexpo The Box, more than 150 companies) is the largest job fair; the Big Four and the EIB announce their own intakes and events on their careers pages, and ADEM organised 106 job fairs in 2025.
atlas-lu.0054: The Big Four’s hiring peaks in September and January, and the EIB takes trainees in March-April and September-October, with intakes announced about 4 months ahead.
atlas-lu.0055: The pages read name no degree level for entry roles: the EIB takes final-year students and graduates with less than 1 year of work experience, and the Big Four take graduates into audit and advisory. A master’s is common but not the stated condition.
atlas-lu.0056: Recognition matters for regulated professions; for other jobs employers read the degree, and foreign documents may need a certified translation. Expatica names the Ministry of Education, Children and Youth for academic qualifications and the Department for the Recognition of Diplomas for professional ones.
atlas-lu.0057: Employers recruit across the border and abroad, so the CV and the language mix count rather than a short list of schools.
atlas-lu.0058: The graduate route runs through internships and graduate intakes, not dual study; the pages read describe no dual-degree programme for graduates.
atlas-lu.0059: Of 510,990 jobs in 2023, 115,420 were in public administration, defence, education and health (Eurostat). The state recruits by competitive exam in the three administrative languages, and the EIB and the CSSF recruit separately.
